issues.legal_issue: A constitutional challenge to an abolition measure may be refused when the challengers accept the compensation flowing from the abolition for the full benefit period and bring their challenge only after substantial delay.
material_facts: The challenged measure abolished cash grants and provided compensation as a consequence of that abolition.
The petitioners accepted compensation for the full twelve-year period provided by the measure, from 1958 to 1970.
They filed constitutional writ petitions in 1970, after the compensation payments had ended, challenging the abolition under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 of the Constitution.
The compensation provision was integrally connected with the abolition, and the compensation was available only because the grants had been abolished.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused to entertain the challenge because the petitioners had accepted the full benefit of the measure and had approached the Court after inordinate delay. Their acceptance of compensation gave a quietus to their challenge to the abolition.
issues.legal_principle: A claimant cannot accept benefits that flow from an impugned measure and at the same time challenge that measure; where compensation rests on the abolition being challenged, accepting that compensation may foreclose the challenge. A claim brought after inordinate delay may also be refused. The Court distinguished State of Madhya Pradesh v. Ranojirao Shinde & Anr. [1968] 3 S.C.R. 489 because the claimants there approached the High Court soon after the relevant measure was enacted. The challenge here invoked Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and was brought by writ petitions under Article 32.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: The proceeding is a constitutional writ petition challenging a measure that abolished a grant.
predicates.accepted_full_benefit_from_impugned_meas: The challengers accepted the full period of compensation provided as a consequence of the abolition they challenge.
predicates.inordinate_delay: The challengers waited an inordinate time before bringing their challenge.

issues.definition: When challengers bring a constitutional writ challenge after accepting the full benefit flowing from the impugned measure and waiting an inordinate time, the challenge is not entertained.

issues.legal_issue: A court may decline to decide an equality challenge to a severable exemption provision when striking the provision would not benefit the challengers and it may provide them a route to relief.
material_facts: The petitioners argued that a provision allowing the government to exempt certain grants was discriminatory because, in their view, it gave no guidance for exemptions.
The Court considered that the challenged provision was severable from the rest of the measure, so striking it would not benefit the petitioners.
The provision could potentially enable the petitioners to seek exemption, and the government’s representative indicated that some petitioners’ cases would be recommended for consideration.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not decide whether the exemption provision was discriminatory and declined to pass on that submission, observing that striking the provision would not benefit the petitioners and might deprive them of a possible means of obtaining relief.
issues.legal_principle: Where a challenged provision is severable and striking it would not benefit the challengers, particularly when the provision may assist them in seeking relief, the Court may decline to adjudicate the challenge. The petitioners relied on Article 14 of the Constitution, but the Court expressed no conclusion on the merits of that equality claim.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: The proceeding is a constitutional writ petition challenging a legal provision.
predicates.challenged_provision_is_severable: The challenged provision can be separated from the remaining provisions without invalidating them.
predicates.striking_provision_would_not_benefit_cha: Removing the challenged provision would not improve the challengers’ position.
predicates.provision_may_assist_challengers: The challenged provision may provide the challengers a possible route to relief.

issues.definition: If a challenged provision is severable, removing it would not benefit the challengers, and it may assist them in obtaining relief, the court may decline to decide the challenge.
